label: digit 2 input at original position >= 4
explanation: Fires when the token 2 is input during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at position 4 or later. Every such step fires (precision 1.0 on dev). Magnitude rises roughly monotonically with position: about 0.28 of max at t=4, 0.54 at t=5, 0.72 at t=6, 0.88 at t=7, and 0.99 at t=8. The maximum is reached when 2 is the final original token. There is also a very weak tail (about 0.02 of max) when 2 is input at t=3, and it never fires at t<3. It does not fire on any other token, including the digits 0, 1 and 3 (only a handful of stray activations), and never fires on the delimiter or in the copy phase, even when 2 is fed back as an input or emitted as an output.

issues: Reproduced the test scores: precision 1.0, recall 0.924, F1 0.960, mass recall 0.997. The predicate has 0 false positives on test.

All 3398 test misses are the input token 2 at t=3, with activation about 0.01 to 0.03 of max, holding 0.3% of activation mass. That matches the claimed weak tail. Adding t=3 to the predicate gives test precision 0.775 and F1 0.873, consistent with the claim.
The profile confirms the feature is zero on the delimiter and in the copy phase, and zero at t<3. Of 44863 active steps on dev, 44850 have input token 2; the other 13 are scattered letters.
The magnitude-versus-position claim fits the per-t mass shares. Mean activation at t=8 is about 3.2x that at t=4 (claimed 0.99/0.28 = 3.5x).
Minor: about 21% of t=3 inputs of 2 fire, and several shown examples have a digit earlier in the sequence. This tail is negligible in mass and does not count as a systematic gap.
